content.comment_body: After a brief power outage, when [product_name] is powered back on, the program is still present but the Real Time Clock resets to 00. Could this be caused by a problem with the backup battery?

Hi, Typically, [product_name] includes a buffer to cover short power interruptions, lasting up to approximately 80 hours. It sounds like there may be a malfunction with your [product_name]. [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: User describes that while the program remains after a power loss, the Real Time Clock on their [product_name] resets to zero. This suggests either a hardware or battery issue, as the device should buffer through short outages. This loss of time data can negatively affect automated processes.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects the Real Time Clock on [product_name] to keep the correct time during brief power failures, similar to how the program memory is retained.
